processing: The heritage listing gives the main stages as selecting material, reprocessing, steaming and baking, with fixing, rolling and pile fermentation in earlier stages. The steamed tea is pressed hard into bricks and dried.
harvest_season: Not sold by picking date. As with other border brick teas, mature leaf is gathered through the growing season and blended before pressing.
appearance_dry: A firm rectangular brick, dark and even, usually stamped with the 川 mark.
appearance_liquor: Clear orange-red, turning a deeper amber with age.
appearance_wet: Green-brown to dark brown coarse leaf fragments.
taste_profile: A clean, plain aroma and a fairly strong, full flavour, without much astringency when brewed with boiling water.

brewing.notes: Use a tea knife and rinse once. Good in a gaiwan, better in a pot on the stove; Mongolian-style milk tea is the classic use.

vintage_note: Sold by production year as green brick and rice brick, in small modern bricks as well as the larger traditional ones. It is drunk both young and aged, and older bricks cost more. Check that the wrapper names the Zhaoliqiao factory, because the wording of neighbouring brands can look similar.
description:
Zhaoliqiao is both a town in Chibi and the factory that carries on the Yangloudong brick tradition, best known for bricks under the 川 mark. Think of this as the working descendant of the old Dong Cha: same district, same kind of tea, now from one long-established plant.

The craft is on China's national intangible heritage list and is one of the Hubei entries in the 2022 UNESCO listing of traditional Chinese tea processing. Leaf is made into raw dark tea, sorted, steamed and pressed, then dried slowly in the brick.

The heritage description calls the brewed tea green-brown in colour with a clean aroma and a fairly strong taste. It is a daily, sturdy tea, not a showy one. Give it boiling water and let it go long if you like it strong, or simmer it and add milk.

As with other brick teas, look for an intact brick, a stated factory and a date. Some Russian shops sell it as Hei Cha Zhuan or call it a red brick, which is a seller's label and not a separate tea.
history:
The tea began as Yangloudong brick. The factory traces its history back to 1861, by its own reckoning, and holds the China Time-honoured Brand title. After 1949 Yangloudong's factories were merged into a state brick tea plant, which moved to Zhaoliqiao in 1953 and later took the town's name.

The craft is passed on from master to apprentice; one report counts six generations, starting with Wang Chunchen, born in 1855. In 2022 it was included in the UNESCO listing of traditional Chinese tea processing. The factory also houses a museum devoted to the 川 tea, reported as the first brick tea museum in China.
